title: UK car industry to press EU for two-year delay to Brexit EV tariffs
extract: UK carmakers are preparing to seek a two-year delay to the EU-UK battery rules of origin that would otherwise trigger 10% tariffs on many electric vehicles from 1 January. Manufacturers argue that European battery production is not yet at the scale needed to meet the rules.

title: Faxes, phones and Bluetooth: Microsoft outage forces businesses to find fixes
extract: A worldwide Microsoft 365 outage disrupted Outlook, Teams and Copilot, forcing businesses, exchanges and financial firms to fall back on telephones, fax machines and Bluetooth transfers. The incident has renewed calls for tested contingency plans and less dependence on a small number of technology providers.

title: China's $3 billion-plus pipeline of Nvidia-powered AI data centres
extract: A Reuters review identified more than $3 billion in Chinese computing projects built around Nvidia processors, including proposed facilities using H100 and H200 systems. The projects show the continuing role of US-designed accelerators in China's AI infrastructure despite export restrictions.

title: Apache HTTP Server patches critical HTTP/2 remote code execution flaw
extract: The Apache Software Foundation has fixed a critical race condition in mod_http2 that could let an unauthenticated attacker corrupt heap memory and execute code with the web server's privileges. The flaw affects Apache HTTP Server 2.4.55 through 2.4.70 when HTTP/2 is enabled.

title: New Windows SignDrop zero-day gives hackers SYSTEM privileges
extract: A newly disclosed flaw in the Windows Common Log File System can reportedly let a local attacker gain SYSTEM privileges by abusing the way privileged processes create authentication files. The researcher says there is no patch yet and that the issue can undermine antimalware self-protection.

title: Police dismantle Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC malware infrastructure
extract: A multinational Operation Endgame action coordinated by Europol and Eurojust seized 257 domains and 235 servers linked to three major malware operations. Investigators also identified 6.4 million stolen victim datasets on the criminal infrastructure.

title: Rare co-founder rescues a Conker banner from the company's former HQ after almost 30 years
extract: Rare co-founder Tim Stamper returned to the developer's original Manor Farm headquarters and removed a Conker promotional banner that had remained in a former studio barn for at least 27 years. The find offers a rare glimpse into the company's history and a piece of memorabilia that may now be preserved.

title: Shigeru Miyamoto reflects on Game Boy creator Gunpei Yokoi
extract: A newly translated 1997 interview captures Shigeru Miyamoto and other Nintendo staff reflecting on Gunpei Yokoi's influence. Miyamoto discusses Yokoi's design philosophy, his work on Game & Watch and the Game Boy, and the ideas behind his approach to game design.

title: Super Mario 64 Gaeilge translation project appears close to completion
extract: A fan translation of Super Mario 64 is nearing completion, bringing Gaeilge to the N64 classic's menus, HUD and in-game text. The project is playable from beginning to end and is now undergoing careful proofreading to improve the accuracy of the translation.

title: Super Metroid x Castlevania fangame brings Samus to Dracula's castle
extract: Metroidvania: Symphony of the Hunter is a fan-made crossover that places Super Metroid's Samus in Castlevania: Symphony of the Night's Dracula's castle. Developed over 12 years, it adds original art, animation, lore, save stations and an escape sequence, and is nearing completion.

title: NES horror homebrew All Hell Unleashed receives its final major update
extract: The Ultimate Edition of the NES homebrew horror tribute adds a killer mode, two-player support and quality-of-life improvements. The project combines characters and themes from classic slasher films and has been developed and updated by a fan team for nearly three years.

title: Does M John Harrison's Booker win mean science fiction is finally accepted by the literary establishment?
extract: M John Harrison's Booker Prize win has prompted leading writers including Kazuo Ishiguro and Jeff VanderMeer to revisit the literary establishment's historic resistance to science fiction. The article explores how Harrison's genre-blending novel The End of Everything challenges the boundaries between literary and speculative fiction.

title: Lighting up the room with the Fortis Novonaut N-42 TR series
extract: Fortis has added three Novonaut N-42 TR models with fully luminous dials designed to maximise visibility in low-light conditions. The new variants bring a striking high-visibility treatment to the brand's space- and tool-watch-inspired chronograph line.

title: Zenith G.F.J. Calibre 135 Double Signed with J.N. Shapiro
extract: Zenith's 25-piece rose-gold G.F.J. collaboration pairs the historic hand-wound Calibre 135 with J.N. Shapiro's hand-turned guilloché dial work and American-style damaskeening on the movement bridges. The limited edition brings independent artisanal decoration to one of watchmaking's most celebrated chronometer movements.

title: Vacheron Constantin adds two new references to the Fiftysix collection
extract: Vacheron Constantin has added two steel Fiftysix references with grey two-tone dials: a time-and-date model and a complete calendar with moonphase. The article also examines the collection's movement sourcing, finishing and positioning within the brand.

title: Disney unveils Star Wars 50th anniversary plans, including an IMAX re-release
extract: Disney and Lucasfilm are planning a yearlong Star Wars 50th anniversary celebration in 2027, including a restored theatrical return of the original 1977 film in IMAX and other formats. The programme also includes commemorative Lego and Hasbro collections, an exhibition and new immersive experiences.
